decisions.reason: The optional splash guard or bowl lip does not necessarily change the established quick-removal and swapping behavior; the source separately addresses cleaning access, which is already represented.
Splash containment is an independent operating constraint and does not change the candidate's strong, frothy texture target, which is already updated by the same message.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY covering the clean, controlled, non-sputtering solenoid pour; the splash-guard decision adds no further dispensing-state change.

The client asks for splash-control provisions to be considered before the BOM is finalized, so the existing same-message component-selection update should also capture evaluation of a guard or bowl lip.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry — I went through the BOM and overall I really like the direction. This is exactly what I was hoping for.

A few thoughts I’d like your input on before we move forward:

• Motors — I’m wondering if 200 RPM might be a bit low for achieving a strong, frothy matcha texture. Do you think it makes sense to increase RPM while still maintaining enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — would a stainless steel or milk-frother-style head perform better than the resin whisk in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality?

• Spout — I’d like to stick with the solenoid approach. It’s important that the pour is clean, controlled, and seamless (mix → open → pour) both for texture and the overall visual experience.

• Splash / mess control — this is really important for events. I want to make sure:
– minimal to no splashing during mixing
– smooth, controlled flow from the spout (no sputtering)
– no dripping when the valve is closed
– good sealing so nothing leaks into the base
– some form of splash guard or lip around the bowl if needed

• Cleaning — I’d like the bowls and spout components to be easy to clean or removable if possible.

Everything else looks great to me. Curious to hear your thoughts on these and if you’d adjust anything before we finalize the BOM.

value_updates.motor_selection_criteria: evaluate whether motor speed should exceed 200 RPM to achieve a strong, frothy texture while maintaining enough torque for smooth mixing
value_updates.whisk_selection_criteria: evaluate stainless-steel or milk-frother-style heads against the resin whisk for consistency, durability, and foam quality
value_updates.splash_control_selection_criteria: evaluate whether a splash guard or lip around the bowl is needed to achieve minimal to no splashing during mixing

decisions.reason: A conditional splash guard or lip does not change the established 2.5-quart capacity, deep-well form, or selected bowl-size reference.
The splash-control change concerns mixing containment and does not alter the spout's location, orientation, construction, or appearance.
The splash-control decision does not change the beige primary color or green accents.
The splash-control decision has no effect on the machine name, retained wording, or customer-facing placard placement.
Adding a splash-control policy does not change the established DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity.
The source conditionally permits a splash guard or lip if needed but does not select a definite geometry or explicitly modify the system-layout or CAD deliverable.
The splash-control change does not determine whether a guard or lip must be custom-made and therefore does not alter the existing V1 sourcing policy.
The message reiterates that liquid must not leak into the base, but the candidate already requires sealing against base and electronics leakage, so its state remains unchanged.
